Our Mission

We are a supportive community helping individuals of all backgrounds find true joy and meaning in life through the teachings of Rebbe Nachman of Breslov.

At the heart of our mission is a commitment to unconditional love and respect for every human being. Regardless of any past experiences or present circumstances, we believe that every human being is worthy of happiness, fulfillment, and inner peace.

Our Vision

We strive to empower individuals to live a life of purpose and fulfillment. We deeply seek to build a global community of love, respect and compassion where every person is supported and uplifted. At Tzion Breslov, we acknowledge life’s challenges and give people the capacity to accept and work through them, with genuine support and real friendship.

Meet Rabbi David Yisrael Kalmus.

Motivational speaker, global educator, licensed master’s social worker, substance abuse counselor, and life coach. His simple yet profound approach has empowered countless individuals to achieve true happiness in their life.

Rooted in the teachings of Rebbe Nachman of Breslov, Rabbi Kalmus’ wisdom will inspire you to live your best life.

How it all began

Rabbi Kalmus speaks:

I grew up in New Jersey to two very loving and unconditionally supportive parents. I was raised in a secular community receiving a public education. Judaism and spirituality was not an essential part of my life until after I had completed my undergraduate education, immediately prior to starting my graduate studies. In fact, for most of my adolescence and early adulthood, I was an atheist. I struggled throughout my school years due to a learning disability that made it incredibly difficult to succeed academically. Because of that learning disability, along with the psychological distress which stems from it, I grew up battling a slew of mental health issues including anxiety and depression, as well as bullying from my peers. I spent 6 years studying psychology and social welfare in university in order to help those who were from vulnerable and mitigated backgrounds. Ironically, while I managed to help others in the most trying of circumstances, I still couldn’t help myself.

After a series of unlikely, serendipitous events, I found myself in the Land of Israel when I was 23 years old. I felt like I was home, even though I had never been there. During that trip, I met the girl who would eventually become my wife, and she opened me up to a new experience of Judaism and spirituality which I had never conceived as being possible. Suddenly, I felt the need to learn everything I could. Amongst all of the different aspects of Torah which I merited to learn, Chassidus and Kabbalah spoke the most deeply to me. I devoured every book I could find on Jewish Mysticism.

I got married and moved to Queens where I chanced upon a book titled ‘Likutei Moharan’ written by Rebbe Nachman of Breslov.

I flipped through the pages and felt something strange happening to me. It was as if a spark of electricity ran through my body.

It was as if Rebbe Nachman had written this book just for me. Every word was so profoundly deep. And yet, it was utterly simple. I again felt like I was home, even though I had never been here.

It spoke to my heart and I became absolutely obsessed with it. I spent years learning, meditating, and absorbing every word I could.

But as much as I was captivated by the lessons, they didn’t penetrate fully. The teachings were beautiful and hopeful beyond belief, yet I remained the same melancholy shell of myself. Due to the immense distance between what I was reading and what I was feeling, I sunk into a deep depression. I just couldn’t get out. I tried every form of therapy and psychiatric medication including more extreme variations, such as electric shock therapy. Nothing helped. I was suffering. My wife was suffering. My 2 little kids were suffering. And I ended up in a psych ward.
I had hit rock bottom.

Rabbi Nachman’s teachings were my lifeline during that harrowing time, but Rebbe Nachman’s most essential advice of engaging in a meditative practice known as ‘Hitbodedut’ still alluded me. ‘Hitbodedut’ involves setting aside all distractions, finding a secluded space in total privacy, and talking to G-d in one’s own language, as though speaking to a dear friend (like a spiritual meditation, but without the cross-legged pretzel pose!). I had learnt about Rebbe Nachman’s exhortation to practice ‘Hitbodedut’ for years, but I had never found the courage to apply it.

In a moment of sheer desperation and a real fight for my life, I was compelled to act on the one piece of advice which Rebbe Nachman had so fiercely advocated for all along.

In the lowest moment of my life, sitting alone in a hospital gown, my eyes filled with tears and my heart with heaviness, I finally made a commitment to devote an hour a day to speaking to G-d.

I started talking to G-d right then and there in my hospital bed, pouring my guts out, confiding in Him and expressing for the first time my deepest worries and fears, my greatest hopes and aspirations. No stone was unturned. No skeletons remained hidden. In what ended up becoming a life altering moment, I made a solemn promise. “If You help me get out of here, not just to survive, but to truly live, I will devote the rest of my life to helping others do the same”.

My journey took time, but eventually I began to heal and started helping others just as I had promised.

It began with teaching ‘Likutei Moharan’ to just a few students one evening a week. But soon, those few students became dozens and that one night became four consecutive nights a week.

Despite the growing demand, the hours in a day remained the same. It became clear that this organic grass roots movement needed to evolve from a mere side project into a fully-fledged organization.

And Tzion Breslov was born.

“So refreshing”

Rabbi David Yisrael Kalmus is unlike any other rabbi I have ever met or known.
He brings a refreshing candidness to his Torah teachings, forming his own unique blend of great knowledge and wisdom, which far exceeds that of a man his age, together with the vast teachings of Rabbeinu Nachman.

“He walks the walk”

The classes of Tzion Breslov provide tremendous value. They give over the teachings of Rebbe Nachman in palatable, modern, relatable language. They provide hope, optimism, perseverance, and the tools to get you through the highs and lows of life. Most of all, they’re given by Rav Kalmus, who is walking the walk, embodying the teachings he is giving over, who will go as far as to share his personal story to show you how these teachings play out in day to day life.

Yoni

There’s more to Breslov than meets the eye.

Embrace the true spirit of Breslov.

What is Breslov?

Breslov is an established Chassidic movement within Orthodox Judaism which organically blossomed from the deep wellsprings of Rebbe Nachman’s wisdom, advice, lifelong courage, and unabashed commitment to the search for truth amongst real brotherhood and friendship. It’s teachings and practices are transparent, voluntary and part of a supportive community. The beauty of Breslov is in its genuine acceptance of every Jew regardless of their background or level of religious observance. ‘Breslovers’, as Rebbe Nachman’s disciples are affectionately referred to, are encouraged to stop and ask profound questions about their life’s meaning and purpose, and to then pursue the answers to those questions with authenticity and bravery.

Who is Rebbe Nachman?

Rebbe Nachman was the great grandson of the Jewish spiritual revolutionary known as the “Ba’al Shem Tov”. From a very young age, Rebbe Nachman concealed his inordinate level of Torah scholarship, ingenuity, and spiritual devotion from the public eye, due to his strong desire to never become a public figure. However, over time, Rebbe Nachman’s unique understanding of the human psyche combined with his unyielding commitment to spiritual advancement ultimately proved too distinctive to remain hidden. Rebbe Nachman became the spiritual leader in the city of Breslov, Ukraine at 30 years old. Rebbe Nachman lived until 38 years old when he passed away from his long battle with turberculosis. At his explicit request, Rebbe Nachman was buried in the city of Uman, Ukraine where Jews of all backgrounds and levels of religious observance continue to visit each and every year to experience deep spiritual connection amidst a unique feeling of genuine camaraderie.

What is a “Tzaddik Emet”, an essential Tzaddik?

According to Kabbalah, the inner dimension of Torah, there is a Jewish soul present in every generation who is uniquely capable of leading the entire nation of Israel, providing every single Jewish man and woman in accordance with his or her particular soul root. The Torah’s paradigm for this central figure is paralleled and directly reflected through the unique leadership of Moses as he guided every Jewish soul out of psycho-spiritual exile and into the “The Land of Israel”. The Jewish Mystics reveal that “The Land of Israel” is an elevated state of consciousness in which G-dliness suffuses and unites all the disparate aspects of one’s personal life, drawing blessing, life force, and harmony in its wake. When Rebbe Nachman speaks about the Tzaddik Emet, the essential Tzaddik, he is referring to that unique person in every generation who most embodies these above mentioned qualities.

What is Uman Rosh HaShana?

Rebbe Nachman explains that every spiritual master or Tzaddik who ever lived has a unique understanding and grasp of one specific area as it relates to spiritual life. One spiritual master may have a unique grasp of Torah, the spiritual wisdom passed down from teacher to student since the inception the Jewish People three thousand years ago. Another may have a novel apprehension of prayer, the essential spiritual mechanism for relating to G-d on a personal level.

Rebbe Nachman stated that his personal, unique understanding is in the realm of renewal. It has been well documented that each time a person saw Rebbe Nachman, he was imbued with a brand new energy and life force. Rebbe Nachman persistently championed the idea of constant renewal, beginning anew, and starting over. Rosh HaShana, the Jewish New Year, is the day which most embodies this phoenix-like spirit. As a result, Rebbe Nachman has a unique connection and affinity for this day. In fact, Rebbe Nachman once said, “My whole mission is Rosh HaShana.”

Due to the tremendous passion and immense meaning with which Rebbe Nachman imbued into his Rosh HaShana, students of Rebbe Nachman over the past two centuries have made it an essential priority to spend this special day in the location and at the burial place of the Rebbe who most embodied its spirit. Uman Rosh HaShana has organically transformed into a place and time of spiritual awakening for Jews of every background and level of religious observance.
